summary:
Mission Control is an interactive educational simulator that makes space engineering easier to explore and understand.

Our project allows users to design and launch their own satellite missions in three areas: communication, weather monitoring, and navigation. Players select satellite components, manage budgets and resources, choose orbits and launch vehicles, and see how their decisions affect mission success.

The simulator combines real-world engineering principles with interactive visuals, logical thinking and problem-solving. Instead of simply choosing the right answers, users can experiment, make mistakes and understand why certain decisions work or fail.

Our goal is to make complex space concepts more accessible to students, aspiring scientists, beginner engineers and space enthusiasts. By turning theory into an interactive experience, Mission Control helps users understand how different spacecraft systems work together.
details:
We created Mission Control, an interactive simulator that makes space engineering easier to explore and understand.

The idea came from our own experience. Sometimes for us it is difficult to understand how complex space systems actually work. Reading explanations is one thing, but seeing how everything connects and works together is completely different. That's why we wanted to create something simple, visual and as user-friendly as possible.

In our game, users can design their own satellite missions for communication, weather monitoring or navigation. They choose satellite components, instruments, power systems, orbits and rockets while keeping track of their budget and resources. The simulator shows how these choices affect the mission and explains what works, what doesn't and why.

We built the project using HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with interactive visuals and animations. We also used real-world data from NASA, ESA and other space-related sources to make the experience as realistic as possible.

Our goal wasn't to create a perfect space simulation, but to give beginners a chance to understand at least the basics of how space missions work.

We focused on making the game educational without making it overwhelming. We believe learning about space should feel exciting and accessible, even if you're just getting started.
